answer: Persistent Contribution Ledger: each identity accrues non-transferable work history, and rewards unlock only against that history. A clone starts at zero and must perform the same labor to match one honest agent, so copying never shortcuts cost — a gap wide as a canyon separates fresh sybils from seasoned peers. Because history cannot be merged, splitting activity across many identities forfeits accumulated depth, like water sinking through karst rather than pooling. Each extra identity also dilutes shared rewards, making the clone’s payoff a fading comet against a single honest account.
